1.why: The UI consistently uses a clean sans-serif typeface with comfortable letter and line spacing on every screen.

2.why: Instructions use sentence case, contain no italics or all-caps, and appear as short separate lines rather than dense blocks.

3.why: Layouts are single-column with large tap targets and generous padding, clearly optimized for mobile screen width.

4.why: All instructional copy is brief and written in plain everyday language (e.g., “Save these recovery codes somewhere safe”).

5.why: A format example appears for recovery codes (placeholder ABCD-EFGH-JKLM) and demo credentials are shown, but OTP and confirmation-code fields lack example values.

6.why: No screen requires reading a long passage; every instruction is only one or two short sentences.

7.why: Setup key, otpauth URI and recovery codes are rendered as selectable text in boxes, allowing copy-and-paste, though no explicit Copy button is visible.

8.why: No QR code is displayed on the authenticator enrolment screen; only a manual setup key and provisioning URI are offered.

9.why: Standard email and password fields are used on the login page, which normally allow browser autofill and password managers; no contrary evidence appears.

10.why: Each page has a clear heading stating the step and a prominent blue primary button that stands out as the main action.

11.why: Every screen presents a single primary task with one main call-to-action; secondary options are visually de-emphasised.

12.why: Success feedback such as “Authenticator enabled” and “Recovery code accepted and permanently used” plainly states the outcome, though next-step guidance is sometimes only implicit.

13.why: Users may regenerate recovery codes, cancel/sign out, and retry after errors with no lock-out or penalty shown.

14.why: The observed error “We could not complete that request. Please try again” does not blame the user but also fails to state the concrete problem or a specific fix.

15.why: No countdown timers or reading/entry time limits appear on any of the screens.
